alternatives.design: Use active pumping instead of passive filtration — pump CSF out while retaining therapeutic via closed-loop feedback
alternatives.technically_easier: NO — active pump is more complex, requires power, higher failure modes
alternatives.cerevasc_could_build: NO — CereVasc has no pump expertise
alternatives.destroys_moat: YES — active pump is a different product category
alternatives.claims_should_cover: YES — file claims on active pumping with retention

alternatives.design: Use charge-based retention instead of size-selective — membrane with charge selectivity (anionic for cationic therapeutics)
alternatives.technically_easier: MARGINAL — charge-selective membranes exist but are less mature than size-selective
alternatives.destroys_moat: NO — still a retention mechanism, just different selectivity
alternatives.claims_should_cover: YES — file claims on charge-based retention

alternatives.design: Apply to VP (ventriculoperitoneal) shunt instead of eShunt
alternatives.technically_easier: YES — VP shunts are standard, larger market
alternatives.cerevasc_could_build: NO — CereVasc is endovascular-focused; VP is a different company's domain
alternatives.destroys_moat: PARTIAL — covers different market segment but doesn't block endovascular competitors
alternatives.claims_should_cover: MAYBE — file broad claims covering all shunt types if possible

alternatives.design: Pulsed drainage — drain CSF in pulses, retaining therapeutic between pulses
alternatives.destroys_moat: NO — still achieves retention, just intermittently
alternatives.claims_should_cover: YES — file claims on pulsed/intermittent drainage

alternatives.design: External filtration — filter CSF outside the body via a percutaneous access port
alternatives.technically_easier: NO — external access increases infection risk
alternatives.claims_should_cover: NO — too different from implant claim

alternatives.design: Use a hydrogel that swells to retain therapeutic but allows CSF diffusion
alternatives.claims_should_cover: YES — file claims on hydrogel-based retention

alternatives.design: Use affinity-based retention — membrane with immobilized antibodies/ligands that bind specific therapeutics
alternatives.technically_easier: NO — affinity membrane is complex, target-specific
alternatives.destroys_moat: PARTIAL — works only for specific therapeutics, not broad retention
alternatives.claims_should_cover: YES — file claims on affinity-based retention

summary.moat_assessment: The claim is reasonably defensible against DA1 (active pump — different category) and DA5 (external — different category). DA2 (charge-based), DA4 (pulsed), DA6 (hydrogel), and DA7 (affinity) are alternative retention mechanisms that should be covered by continuation claims. DA3 (VP shunt) is a different market segment and should be covered by broad claims. The territory-level moat requires filing continuations covering DA2, DA4, DA6, DA7 mechanisms.
summary.territory_level_moat_achievable: PARTIAL — requires continuation claims; not automatic from the base claim
